Part One Institutionalization
Article 23

Article 12
The provision of integrated services to women victims of violence shall be carried out free of charge, quickly, safely, empathetically, without discrimination, easily accessible, and with a guarantee of confidentiality.

CHAPTER X
MONITORING, EVALUATION AND REPORTING
Article 27
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection in the Region.
(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically from the planning stage through the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection for the current year.
(4) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
(5) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the following year.
(6) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of integrated services for the Protection of women victims of violence to the Governor with a copy submitted to the minister in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs, and the minister in charge of home affairs.
(7) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of the establishment and development of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions in an integrated manner to the minister in charge of home affairs with a copy to the minister in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(8) The implementation of reporting as referred to in paragraph (6) and paragraph (7) shall be conducted annually and/or when necessary.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Government is the Central Government.
2. Governor is the Governor of South Sulawesi Province.
3. Region is Luwu Regency.
4. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
5. Regent is the Regent of Luwu.
6. Gender is a concept that refers to roles and responsibilities as women and as men that are created and internalized in families, communities and community culture in which we live including expectations, attitudes, characteristics, behavior of how to be a man and how to be a woman.
7. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, resulting in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or human rights and basic freedoms in the use of rights in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
8. Women's empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, temporarily or courts or other parties either based on court decisions.
10. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or causes deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations.
12. Regional Cooperation is an agreement between governor and governor or governor and regent/mayor or between regent/mayor and other regent/mayor, and or governor, regent/mayor with third parties, made in writing and giving rise to rights and obligations.

may conduct supervision of the implementation of the protection of women from acts of violence carried out by the regional government by submitting aspirations to the Regent or the DPRD.

Article 2

a. respect for human rights;
b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and
d. protection of victims.

CHAPTER VII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 22
(1) The community may participate in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. Responses and input in policy formulation;
b. cooperation; and/or
c. complaints/reports.
(4) The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Second Part Handling
Article 10
The target of handling as referred to in Article 4 letter b is every woman.

Article 8
The target of prevention as referred to in Article 4 letter a is every woman.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Protection of Women is implemented based on the principles of:
a. respect for human rights;
b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and
d. protection of victims.

Article 5

CHAPTER VIII
INSTITUTIONALIZATION, GUIDANCE, AND SUPERVISION
Part One Institutionalization
Article 23
(1) Handling as referred to in Article 11 shall be carried out in an integrated manner by relevant SKPD and/or service institutions that handle the protection of women from acts of violence.
(2) The implementation of integrated services shall be coordinated by BPPKB or other name as further regulated by Regent Regulation.
(3) The implementation of integrated services shall be in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 12
The provision of integrated services to women victims of violence shall be carried out free of charge, quickly, safely, empathetically, without discrimination, easily accessible, and with a guarantee of confidentiality.

Part Three Supervision
Article 24

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Government is the Central Government.
2. Governor is the Governor of South Sulawesi Province.
3. Region is Luwu Regency.
4. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
5. Regent is the Regent of Luwu.
6. Gender is a concept that refers to roles and responsibilities as women and as men that are created and internalized in families, communities and community culture in which we live including expectations, attitudes, characteristics, behavior of how to be a man and how to be a woman.
7. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, resulting in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or human rights and basic freedoms in the use of rights in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
8. Women's empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, temporarily or courts or other parties either based on court decisions.
10. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or causes deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations.
12. Regional Cooperation is an agreement between governor and governor or governor and regent/mayor or between regent/mayor and other regent/mayor, and or governor, regent/mayor with third parties, made in writing and giving rise to rights and obligations.

CHAPTER VII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 22
(1) The community may participate in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. Responses and input in policy formulation;
b. cooperation; and/or
c. complaints/reports.
(4) The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

BAB V
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
First Part Prevention
Article 8
The target of prevention as referred to in Article 4 letter a is every woman.

CHAPTER X
MONITORING, EVALUATION AND REPORTING
Article 27
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection in the Region.
(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically from the planning stage through the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection for the current year.
(4) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
(5) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the following year.
(6) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of integrated services for the Protection of women victims of violence to the Governor with a copy submitted to the minister in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs, and the minister in charge of home affairs.
(7) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of the establishment and development of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions in an integrated manner to the minister in charge of home affairs with a copy to the minister in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(8) The implementation of reporting as referred to in paragraph (6) and paragraph (7) shall be conducted annually and/or when necessary.

Second Part Handling
Article 10
The target of handling as referred to in Article 4 letter b is every woman.

Article 13
The integrated service provider is obligated to provide services in accordance with the service principles as referred to in Article 12.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Government is the Central Government.
2. Governor is the Governor of South Sulawesi Province.
3. Region is Luwu Regency.
4. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
5. Regent is the Regent of Luwu.
6. Gender is a concept that refers to roles and responsibilities as women and as men that are created and internalized in families, communities and community culture in which we live including expectations, attitudes, characteristics, behavior of how to be a man and how to be a woman.
7. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, resulting in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or human rights and basic freedoms in the use of rights in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
8. Women's empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, temporarily or courts or other parties either based on court decisions.
10. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or causes deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations.
12. Regional Cooperation is an agreement between governor and governor or governor and regent/mayor or between regent/mayor and other regent/mayor, and or governor, regent/mayor with third parties, made in writing and giving rise to rights and obligations.

CHAPTER XI
PROHIBITIONS AND SANCTIONS
Article 28
Any person who intentionally commits violence against women shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the laws and regulations.

MONITORING, EVALUATION AND REPORTING
Article 27
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection in the Region.
(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically from the planning stage through the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection for the current year.
(4) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
(5) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the following year.
(6) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of integrated services for the Protection of women victims of violence to the Governor with a copy submitted to the minister in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs, and the minister in charge of home affairs.
(7) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of the establishment and development of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions in an integrated manner to the minister in charge of home affairs with a copy to the minister in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(8) The implementation of reporting as referred to in paragraph (6) and paragraph (7) shall be conducted annually and/or when necessary.

CHAPTER X
MONITORING, EVALUATION AND REPORTING
Article 27
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection in the Region.
(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically from the planning stage through the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection for the current year.
(4) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
(5) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the following year.
(6) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of integrated services for the Protection of women victims of violence to the Governor with a copy submitted to the minister in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs, and the minister in charge of home affairs.
(7) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of the establishment and development of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions in an integrated manner to the minister in charge of home affairs with a copy to the minister in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(8) The implementation of reporting as referred to in paragraph (6) and paragraph (7) shall be conducted annually and/or when necessary.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Protection of Women is implemented based on the principles of:
a. respect for human rights;
b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and
d. protection of victims.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Government is the Central Government.
2. Governor is the Governor of South Sulawesi Province.
3. Region is Luwu Regency.
4. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
5. Regent is the Regent of Luwu.
6. Gender is a concept that refers to roles and responsibilities as women and as men that are created and internalized in families, communities and community culture in which we live including expectations, attitudes, characteristics, behavior of how to be a man and how to be a woman.
7. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, resulting in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or human rights and basic freedoms in the use of rights in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
8. Women's empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, temporarily or courts or other parties either based on court decisions.
10. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or causes deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations.
12. Regional Cooperation is an agreement between governor and governor or governor and regent/mayor or between regent/mayor and other regent/mayor, and or governor, regent/mayor with third parties, made in writing and giving rise to rights and obligations.

Article 25
may conduct supervision of the implementation of the protection of women from acts of violence carried out by the regional government by submitting aspirations to the Regent or the DPRD.

CHAPTER VII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 22
(1) The community may participate in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. Responses and input in policy formulation;
b. cooperation; and/or
c. complaints/reports.
(4) The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

PROHIBITIONS AND SANCTIONS
Article 28
Any person who intentionally commits violence against women shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the laws and regulations.
